summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (for later Q&A; compact, not verbatim)

## BOOK 1 — *Pharos, the Egyptian* (Guy Boothby, 1899, D. Appleton & Co.)
**Frame/Preface:** Letter from Sir William Betford (Bampton St. Mary, Dorset) to George Trevelyan (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Betford's servant Jenkins announces "Silver" (Honoré de Silva), servant of Cyril Forrester, at ~7pm, Dec 14 ("18--"). De Silva brings a packet; Betford writes a receipt ("THE GRANGE, BAMPTON ST. MARY"). De Silva says Forrester "will never return," wants to be considered dead. Forrester's letter enclosed (asks Betford & Trevelyan to publish his manuscript; P.S. Matthew Simpford, Strand, holds two pictures). Betford reads manuscript until 5:15am. "Six months later" they publish.

**Ch I–II (Forrester narrates):** Painter Cyril Forrester; father a famous Egyptologist. Last week of March, painted Merenptah/Pharaoh & magicians picture for Academy (his 8th). Walk with Betford & Trevelyan; midnight near Villiers St. Begging man threatens suicide at Hungerford Bridge. At Cleopatra's Needle, drowning man ("Help!") swept past steps; stranger (Pharos) laughs and doesn't rescue. Forrester seizes him: "Are you a man or a fiend." Pharos: small, ivory/corpse-coloured skin, deep sunken eyes, fur coat, skull cap, stick, age 70–100. Vanishes toward Charing Cross.
June (Friday early): Merridew family (George Merridew, wife, son at Oxford, tennis-champion daughter, Gwendoline, Ethel) visit studio; Academy. Pharos appears with woman (Valerie de Vocxqal, Hungarian violinist, Lady Medenham's protégée; "Fräulein"). Forrester faints. Medenham House "at home" in Eaton Square: Valerie plays violin (her own composition, despairing/tarantella). Introduced to Pharos by Lady Medenham; Pharos expresses interest in Forrester's picture.

**Ch III:** Pharos enters Forrester's studio at 1am (Venetian lamp, mummy-case of Ptahmes, Chief of King's Magicians, under Menptah; father stole it). Pharos wants mummy; hypnotises Forrester who loses consciousness.

**Ch IV:** Dawn; police inspector: murder of curio dealer (Clausand/ "Herman Clausand" in Bonwell St., old curiosity shop at corner) ~midnight–1am; man seen entering alley near Forrester's house. Forrester lies to protect Pharos. Mummy gone. Lady Medenham tells Valerie's story (father Hungarian noble killed in duel; home mortgaged; Pharos adopted her ~7 yrs). Sir George Legrath (Director, Egyptian Museum; old friend of Forrester's father) — reveals Pharos left for Naples; gives card of "Carlo Angelotti, Public Letter-writer, arches of Theatre San Carlo, Naples."

**Ch V:** Naples (summer). Angelotti (sells violins now) denies knowing Pharos; Forrester sees Valerie in carriage. Note at hotel: meet Pharos at Temple of Mercury, Pompeii, 4pm.

**Ch VI:** Pompeii. Pharos denies murder; confesses taking mummy by hypnosis; newspaper confession of German Johann Schmidt (suicide at Bow Street) for Clausand murder. Pharos' tour of Pompeii (Temple of Isis, house of Tullus Agrippa, murder by gladiator Tymon). Invites Forrester to dine.

**Ch VII:** Pharos's house in Naples (courtyard, Renaissance paintings; Forrester's own painting). Baden story (nobleman ruined, daughter paralysed, suicide at Kursaal). Valerie warns "this place is fatal." Dinner: Pharos eats only fruit, small cakes, powder in water. Monkey Pehtes. Cigarettes (Turkish, drug-like). Pharos proposes Egypt trip on steam-yacht; Forrester agrees. Valerie begs him to flee; he refuses unless she comes; she refuses.

**Ch VIII:** Yacht at Naples. Overheard Pharos hypnotising Valerie ("thou seest…" plague/death vision). Storm chapter IX: Pharos cowers in fear; Valerie says he is "not human."

**Ch X–XI:** Port Said, Cairo (Hotel). Valerie's story of earlier escapes (St. Petersburg/Norway; Buda-Pesth; Norwegian fjord; a pianist's suicide). Forrester follows Pharos to Great Pyramid; trapped in Queen's Chamber; hypnotised/dosed at Sphinx; "vision" of Ptahmes (Pharos = Ptahmes). Nile steamer, Luxor. Pharos recounts Ptahmes history.

**Ch XII–XIII:** Painting shown to Valerie; Pharos "Heaven only knows" line. Pharos meets envoy Salem Awad at Luxor. Night in Karnak temple, subterranean hall, old man in white (Paduamen-like guide), kriosphinxes, mummies; Forrester sees Ptahmes' burial vision (Harmachis; Amen-Ra; "rise, Ptahmes"). Pharos bedside; Forrester ill with plague (spot on left arm).

**Ch XIV:** Itinerary: London June 7; Naples June 10; Cairo June 18; Karnak June 27; Constantinople; Vienna; Prague July 15 (Teyn Kirche). Valerie confesses love for Forrester; they plan escape. Plague news in newspaper. Concert at palace before Emperor Franz Josef; Count de Schelyani.

**Ch XV–XVI:** Escape from Prague (6:15 train), Dresden, Berlin (Herr Schuncke's restaurant; Ludwig), Wittenberge, Hamburg (Hôtel Continental, "Mr. and Miss Clifford"). Steamship office: no boats to England (plague). Valerie falls ill (Pharos hypnotic). Forrester runs for prescription: chemists (Dittmer—Forrester gives gold watch); Pharos returns with medicine. Pharos reveals he followed them by train. Captain Wisemann (Hamburg, giant with huge ears), steamer *Margrave of Brandenburg*.

**Ch XVII–XVIII:** Voyage; plague on ship (steward, cook, captain dies—captain's throat swelling). Land at night near Tebworth; train to Norwich; Liverpool Street; Park Lane house (once Lord Tollingtower's).

**Ch XIX–XX:** Duchess of Amersham's ball; Antiquarian Club; Covent Garden fancy ball; thieves' den at Seven Dials; Pharos reveals he deliberately spread plague. Forrester learns (via statistician in club) that plague-carriers attended those events. Forrester confronts Pharos; Pharos reveals he is Ptahmes; hypnotises Forrester to sleep.

**Ch XXI:** Five/six days hypnotic sleep; Forrester wakes; goes to Home Office (Sir Edward Grangerfield) – disbelieved; Valerie finds him in St James's Park; Pharos dying in Park Lane (Valerie's trance vision of Paduamen; Pharos chokes himself; monkey dies). Forrester's brain fever; wakes in yacht cabin with Valerie: "Pharos is dead." Final line: sunlight through porthole.

**Ending advertisements:** Boothby's other novels: Dr. Nikola, Lust of Hate, Beautiful White Devil, Bid for Fortune, Marriage of Esther.

Key names: Cyril Forrester; Sir William Betford; George Trevelyan; Honoré de Silva; Pharos/Ptahmes; Valerie de Vocxqal/Vocsqal; Lady Medenham; Lord Medenham; Sir George Legrath; Carlo Angelotti; Salem Awad; Herman Clausand; Jenkins (servant); Merridews; Count de Schelyani; Herr Schuncke; Captain Wisemann; Duchess of Amersham; Sir Edward Grangerfield; Matthew Simpford.

## BOOK 2 — *When Freemen Shall Stand* (Nelson S. Bond, Fantastic Adventures Nov 1943, Gutenberg 74576)
**Ch I:** Lab of Stephen "Steve" Duane (chemist, Lieutenant) & assistant Sgt. Chuck Lafferty. Testing new anesthetic gas *methioprane* (from swamp-musk seed-pod). Nazi spy Eric von Rath (guttural, .44 pistol) opens door; demands vial; Chuck drops flask; gas. Both men and von Rath frozen (catalepsy) in glass dome. Wakened centuries later (Chuck's body cold like marble; catalepsy). Clothing: gold loincloth/metal harness, doeskin sandals.

**Ch II:** Women of the Tucki Clan (Fautnox = Fort Knox, KY); Priestess **Beth** (dust-gold hair, golden breast-cups); Mother **Maatha**. Warrior captain **Jain**. Men are pets/breeders; Women rule. Sacrifice of pet male at glass altar; Steve stops it. US anthem mangled ("Daan's surly light"). Venus = Daan (Venusians "Daans").

**Ch III:** Mother explains Daan invasion (~1000 yrs+; 3488 year now; Steve slept from 1942 — ~1546 years). Legend: Slumberers; "Dwain" (Steve), evil one must die; von Rath says he's ally. Mount Rushmore = "Place of the Gods" (Jarg, Taamuz, Ibrim, Tedhi = Washington, Jefferson, Lincoln, Roosevelt-analog). Plan: gather allies; Steve's secret = methioprane.

**Ch IV–V:** Wild Ones (male tribe, leader **Jon**). Battle; "Men are men" revelation; Ancient records (Women vs Men war). Steve's "Revelation." Beth chooses Steve as mate. Marriage talk. Steve refuses to take advantage (Chuck teases).

**Ch VI–VIII:** Journey to Cincinnati (Sinnaty; "Nedlunplaza" = Netherland Plaza; Carew Tower). Daan captured; Rodrik of Mish-kin (blond Brother) — Steve beats him in fight; Rodrik made "Brother." Overlord **Loala** (silver hair, silver-grey eyes, woman Overlord); Loala's advisors Malgro and Okuno; Brotherhood (human collaborators); Treatment (brain pattern cylinder). Loala offers Steve a bargain.

**Ch IX–XII:** Steve given brain-pattern device; Rodrik spy; Steve learns Okuno (real = human Wiam of Kleevlun, disguised). Rebellion at Loovil; Beth's warriors; Louisville battle; Rodrik sent to Sinnaty; Steve pursues, captured; sentenced; Okuno's trick: Rodrik killed by cylinder destruction; Steve given identity "Captain Huumo."

**Ch XIII–XIV:** Spaceship *Oalumuo*; ten-day voyage; Loala on board; Venus planet described. Slave camp in swamps; Chuck finds swamp-musk (klaar) → methioprane production. Von Rath (recovered) betrays Steve. Loala's bargain offer: Steve's brain replaced. Loala dies (burned by von Rath's ray). Steve gives her "methioprane" sleep. Chuck captures the Daan fleet with gas. Ending: fleet returns to Earth; Steve: "Home!" Beth: "because you are—a man." Final lines: "For a woman always has the last word."

Key names: Steve Duane; Chuck Lafferty; Eric von Rath; Beth; Mother Maatha; Jain; Jon; Rodrik of Mish-kin; Loala; Malgro; Okuno (Wiam); Grudo; Amarro; Thaamo; Jak of Norlinz; Meg and Daiv; Salem? (none).

## BOOK 3 — *The Fatal Three* (M. E. Braddon, 3 vols., Simpkin Marshall; Gutenberg 75410–75412)
**Vol I. Book the First: "Clotho; or Spinning the Thread."**
- Ch I: John Fausset (stout, ~40s, ex-silk merchant; Fausset & Co., St Paul's Churchyard & Lyons) and wife Maud (Hon. Maud Donfrey, dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, 19 at marriage, 9 years married); daughter **Mildred** (7). Fausset asks Maud to adopt orphan **Fay** (14). Mildred intercedes.
- Ch II: Fay arrives at Upper Parchment Street, Mayfair (Grosvenor Sq. area), with Fausset; Mildred and Fay bond; Fay given Bell's room. Fausset's ward; Maud resents her.
- Ch III: **Bell** (Martha Bell, Maud's old nurse, ex-wife of Castle-Connell gardener Patrick Bell) hostile to Fay; Fay's background hinted.
- Ch IV: Fay's school (Miss Constable's, Streatham); Fay expelled. The Hook (Fausset's villa on Thames near Chertsey/Windsor). Mildred's scarlet fever; Fay nurses her. Maud's outburst "your father's daughter"; Fay sent to school in Brussels.
- Ch V–VI (Vol I continued): Mildred's years later; Mildred's mother says Fay was Fausset's natural daughter; Fausset hides his secret.
- Ch VII–IX: **George Greswold** (born George Ransome, son of Squire Ransome of Mapledown, Sussex; mother left him Enderby Manor, Hampshire; he met Mildred at The Hook; married ~14 years before the story; daughter **Lola** (Laura), d. aged 12, of polluted well water/typhoid at Enderby). Greswold's dream "judgment!".
- Ch X: Castellani (César, Milanese adventurer, author of *Nepenthe*, tenor, pianist) meets Greswold/Mildred at Enderby; reveals Greswold's first marriage (to Vivien Faux, in Florence/Nice) — Mildred's shock.
- Ch XI–XII: Mildred demands answers; Castellani pursues her; Pamela Ransome (Greswold's niece, heiress £1500/yr, daughter of Randolph Ransome; flaxen, plump, fox-terrier Box).
- Ch XIII–XIV: Charity concert at Enderby (Castellani sings "Nepenthe"-like). Greswold tells Mildred of first wife; Mildred sees portrait; faints.
- Vol II (Book the Second: "Lachesis"): Mildred flees to Queen Anne's Gate (Mrs. Tomkison, Cecilia). Lawyer Pergament (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Mildred at Brighton with aunt **Gertrude Fausset** (Miss Fausset, Lewes Crescent; church St Edmund's; Vicar Samuel Maltravers). Castellani at Brighton/Pallanza; Pamela charmed. Mildred to Nice; Lady Lochinvar; Villa Montfleuri / Bout du Monde at St. Jean; Maria Castellani (Paolo's cousin, madwoman singer) at asylum (Dr. Leroy). Mildred learns Vivien died at St Jean, pushed/jumped off cliff; George Ransome confined in asylum at St André (Nice).
- Vol II Ch IX: Mildred resolves; Castellani told Mildred George Ransome killed wife.
- Vol III, Book the Third: "Atropos; or That Which Must Be."
- Ch I: Asylum interview; Maria sings. Mildred returns to Nice; Pamela enjoys Nice.
- Ch II: Greswold alone at Enderby; Pamela writes.
- Ch III–V: Vivien Faux's history recounted (George Ransome's first marriage to Vivien; Vivien's jealousy; Ransome's detention; Vivien's death ~April 1868 at St Jean; grave in Villefranche; Mildred's rose-cross planting).
- Ch VI–VIII: Pamela entangled with Malcolm Stuart (Scotch, Lady Lochinvar's nephew); Castellani rejected; Mildred visits Brighton; Miss Fausset's admission: Castellani's father Paolo seduced Fausset in Milan 1848?, secret civil "marriage" (sham), son Fay born, Fausset (John) took Fay as natural daughter; Fay (Fanny, Vivien Faux) given 30,000 *l.*; Miss Fausset's confessed guilt.
- Ch IX: Letters at The Hook (Mildred finds them in father's cupboard: letters from Gertrude to brother John; Mildred's discovery of Fay's true parentage as Gertrude's daughter, not Fausset's—Gertrude was the mother; John Fausset was the protector). Mildred returns to Greswold.
- Ch X–XI: Mildred's return; Greswold forgives; Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey; Miss Fausset dies early winter; Greswold Hospital endowed; Greswold dies; Castellani's fate.

Key names: John Fausset; Maud Fausset (née Donfrey); Mildred (later Greswold); George Greswold (Ransome); Lola (Laura); Fay / Vivien Faux; Martha Bell; Gertrude Fausset (Miss F.); Castellani (César; Paolo, father); Pamela Ransome; Malcolm Stuart; Lady Lochinvar; Mrs. Tomkison (Cecilia); Samuel Maltravers; Clement Cancellor; Rollinson (curate, Enderby); Porter (doctor); Pergament; Dr. Leroy; Maria Castellani; Mrs. Hillersdon (Louise Lorraine); Tom Hillersdon; Box (fox-terrier); Kassandra (setter); Bell's rooms; The Hook; Enderby Manor; Riverdale; Ivy Cottage.
